citations.assessment: Rav prays in Geniva’s house and does not interrupt Yirmeyah bar Abba’s prayer behind him.
Rav Yosef names Geniva in his objection. The immediately preceding report explicitly reads Rav, consistent with Heilprin’s correction.
Geniva reports Rav in connection with the decrees.
This witness gives Ravina in the chain from Geniva and Rav.
The parallel reads Rabbi Avina here and repeats the description of the inner stomach.
Geniva greets each sage as a king and justifies the doubled greeting. In the subsequent reports Rav Yehudah conveys Rav’s ruling.
This reads Rabbi Assi and gives Chiyya bar Abba’s clarification directly from Geniva instead of Heilprin’s printed Nanniva.
Elazar advises restraint and Geniva is put in a neck-chain. The letter’s unnamed tormentors should not all be treated as individually named.
The report specifies 400 zuz for Avina from the wine of Nehar Panya. Its chapter is Haomer, consistent with Heilprin’s correction.
The checked Bavli reads Rav Huna and Rav Chisda, as in Heilprin’s correction. The first speaker is left unnamed.
The gloss explains the contentious designation by reference to the conflict with Mar Ukva.
The second encounter has the same two sages. Geniva transmits Rav’s teaching through Rav Chanan bar Rava.
The fox parable is attributed to Geniva and concerns departure with no more than one brought in.
